chapter: Arrival and the Pete Lala photograph
title: Playing the 1919 World Series and a shooting at a hall down the coast
summary: Willie J. recalls a postcard from a 1919 job and the story of a drunk man shooting through a hall while the bass player got stuck in the rafters.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Yeah, well I had one of, I made, let's see, we played that World Series 1919, and Lawrence Stewart, I lost my copy, and Lawrence Stewart, he gave me a little postcard thing, you know? Yes, that's all. And he reproduced it. Yeah. He had it reproduced. Yeah. I still have it, and I have this one. I kept up with this one, but the other I couldn't. I misplaced it. Yeah.
Yeah. Yeah. We were really, remember Willie, we played down the coast. Who was that?
We played down the coast. Oh. When you had that little run, when the man shot up the hall.
I played in Cessna for you playing in there.

Yeah, and some fella you knew from in the district, you see, an old fella, and they got to talking from back there in, what's that man here, Billy Phillips and them, talking about Billy Phillips and all of them? About the old cabaret and everything happening in the district. So this guy had a mix up with someone, one of the boys down there bought the light, and the dynamo used to keep the supply of the light, and they had a mix up with that. And this fella, man, was half drunk and he'd come shooting through the hall. My daddy had rafters up there. We had Cleo, he got drowned on the 6-0. He got drowned down on the ship. He was a steamship man. And he had his base, got caught up in the ceiling, you know, with the rafters. And he was trying to say, get out the way, Dr. Dunn. Excuse me, go ahead and stand there. I said, where's Papa? Papa, right out almost to the lake. Yeah, he's trying to, almost to the lake. I said, I thought you were such a brave man. He said, no, but he's shooting, Rowling.
